markets.ai_overview_summary: Columns suggested: basics (name, location, contact, date availability, hours), capacity and space, base and add-on costs (rental, ceremony fee, catering and bar, service charges, tax, gratuity, deposit), inclusions and rules (outside caterer, curfew, parking), estimated total at your guest count and a rating score. Cites Reddit advice to put venues in columns, enter $0 for included items and leave unknowns blank. Names WordLayouts free template, The Knot workbook and Etsy paid templates.

cross_market_insights: All four SERPs are dominated by template sellers and aggregators (Etsy, Pinterest, Scribd, Creative Market, Facebook answer pages). Very few editorial pages; only Wedinspire (2023) and The Knot (general planning workbook) are real guides.
Intent is mixed: people want a copyable template first, then help deciding what to put in it. Ranking pages give one or the other, rarely both, and the best templates are paid.
No ranking page explains how to weight columns or turn the sheet into a decision. The NY AI Overview mentions an 'overall rating score' without any method.

No ranking page has columns for a venue abroad: legal ceremony on site, transfers and access, room blocks, currency of quote, local curfew and noise rules, wet-weather plan. Only a US blog (icecreamandneondreams) itemises room blocks for destination venues.
Australian results surface a Victorian venue lead magnet (Bramleigh Estate) in Brisbane; AU pages are domestic. Nobody writes for Australians comparing a Sydney venue with one in Italy or Bali.
US costs language (rentals, gratuity, tax) leaks into AU results; an AUD framing with minimum spend, venue hire and service charges is a local gap.

Volumes: the primary keyword is small in AU (30) and 320 in US. Adjacent 'questions to ask wedding venue' (AU 90, US 2,400) is owned by an existing Wedded Wonderland page, so this piece must link it, not compete. 'wedding planning spreadsheet' (AU 390, US 2,400) has no cluster head on our site.
payload.recommended_angle: The free, copyable venue shortlist tab with destination columns built in: a table readers can paste into Google Sheets or Excel today, a simple weighting method to turn it into a ranked decision, and a section on the columns that only matter abroad (legal ceremony on site, transfers, room blocks, currency, wet weather, curfew), showing the invisible checks a Wedded Advisor runs before a venue earns a row.
